extracted.intended_audience: Indian affairs officials, school administrators, educators, and policymakers (U.S. federal and state) concerned with Indian education and civil-rights protection
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and practical guidance for operating Indian training schools (educational methods, industrial apprenticeship, discipline, health, wages, exhibitions) together with legal/policy guidance for securing Indians' protection under civil law and appropriate legislation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial vocational training per student
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the object to give direction and encouragement to each student of sufficient age in some particular branch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students of suitable age should be assigned to a specific trade or branch, provided directed instruction, and given practical experience; generally work one and a half or two days each week and attend school the other days; mature students who desire proficiency may be kept continuously at work and given night-school instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use competent practical instructors and skilled farm oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Various branches of the mechanic arts have been established, under competent and practical workmen, and a skilled farmer placed in charge of the agricultural department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industrial instruction should be provided by competent, practical workmen and an experienced farmer; supervision must be practical and skilled to ensure useful vocational outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship stability
rubrics_metrics.description: The boys desiring to learn trades have generally been allowed to choose. Once placed at a trade they are not changed, except for extraordinary reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain continuity in apprenticeship assignments to build skill; avoid frequent reassignment unless exceptional circumstances justify it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure production quality against standard mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: Being guided and watched by competent mechanics, the quality of the work turned out challenges comparison with white mechanics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate industrial output (harness, tinware, plows, wagons, woodwork, bread, etc.) by comparing workmanship, durability, and finish to prevailing standards among non-Indian mechanics; committee awarded premiums where work 'compares very favorably with work by pale-face mechanics.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Training girls in household and textile industries
rubrics_metrics.description: The girls have been placed under a system of training in the manufacture and mending of garments, the use of the sewing-machine, laundry work, cooking, and the routine of household duties pertaining to their sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Girls should receive instruction in sewing (including machines), garment manufacture, laundering, cooking, and domestic routines; production of school clothing, underwear, and garments is both training and useful output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibition and assessment principles for industrial work
rubrics_metrics.description: The methods of determining the comparative merits of these exhibits...a new basis of comparison necessary; proficiency reached by short training is to be noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging exhibits, focus on evidence of learning and proficiency (workmanship, aptness, care) rather than only traditional exhibition standards; contrast manufactured articles with relics to demonstrate progress; award premiums for quality, neatness, and practical utility (examples: quilt, shirts, harness, tinware, bread, penmanship).

rubrics_metrics.name: Individualized summer placements
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the authority of the department...two boys and one girl to Lee, Mass., placed in family homes for the summer months...This plan is an individualizing process most helpful to the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange separate family placements during vacations to give students practical living experience, language immersion, and working drills; one-student-per-home placements recommended to maximize learning and integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline via pupil courts for serious offenses
rubrics_metrics.description: When offenses have been serious enough to demand corporal punishment, the cases have generally been submitted to a court of the older pupils, and this has proved a most satisfactory method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve corporal punishment; for serious disciplinary cases, use peer/adjudicative bodies (courts of older pupils) to handle matters, fostering responsibility and satisfactory discipline outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coeducation is acceptable and advantageous
rubrics_metrics.description: No trouble has arisen from the coeducation of the sexes; on the contrary, it has marked advantages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coeducational arrangements are supported and considered beneficial; monitor closely but expect positive social and educational outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military drill to teach discipline and cleanliness
rubrics_metrics.description: The boys have been organized into companies as soldiers...They have been uniformed and drilled in many of the movements of army tactics. This has taught them obedience and cleanliness, and given them a better carriage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use organized drill, uniforming, and company structure to instill obedience, personal cleanliness, and improved bearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music instruction as a rapid skill-building activity
rubrics_metrics.description: A lady friend in Boston gave us a set of brass instruments. Under the direction of a competent instructor, twelve of the boys have in a little over two months learned to play these instruments so as to give us tolerable music for our parades.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce structured music training with competent instructors; even short, intensive courses can yield public-performance-ready results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health monitoring and workload adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: There has been some difficulty...the chief trouble is with their health...They do not thrive as well during the hottest weather, and accordingly the hours of study and labor have been temporarily cut down.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closely monitor student health and be prepared to reduce hours of study and labor during adverse conditions (hot weather, epidemics); track morbidity/mortality and adjust programs to protect vulnerable students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious and community integration
rubrics_metrics.description: All of the boys have been divided into classes, and regularly attend the different Sunday schools of the town...Several of our older and more intelligent boys have become members and scholars. This has been an inestimable benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage participation in local religious institutions and Sunday schools as part of moral training and community integration; foster relationships with local congregations and clergy to support students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Object method and rudimentary curriculum
rubrics_metrics.description: Their studies are rudimentary; teaching is chiefly by the object method. They are now reading simple stories, are eager to learn, and most interesting as pupils.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use object-teaching methods for early instruction, focusing on simple, practical reading, conversational English, and basic composition/letter writing to build usable literacy quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain habits during vacations
rubrics_metrics.description: During the summer there has been almost entire cessation from study, but regular habits and days' works have been kept up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when formal study pauses (e.g., summer), preserve regular work habits and routines to maintain gains made during term time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wage payment policy for student labor
rubrics_metrics.description: After a year's study of the Indians it was thought proper and necessary to pay them in cash for their labor. The amount of wages is based upon the market price of the goods they will need and the number of hours they work, rather than upon the value of the work...large wages to begin with would demoralize them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compensate student labor in cash tied to the market cost of necessary goods and hours worked (not solely 'value' of output); start with modest wages to promote economy and discourage wasteful spending; use wages to teach personal responsibility (e.g., purchasing clothing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade assignment criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: In dividing the work among the boys the first consideration was to have the agencies represented by as many different trades as possible. The second consideration was the boy's physical constitution, and in what trade he would be most likely to excel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign trades to achieve representation of various agencies and to match students' physical constitution and aptitude; consult student preference only when judgment indicates capability, avoiding peer-influenced choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require practical accountability for personal expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of receiving clothing as fast as it was worn out, the boys have been put on wages, out of which they are expected to purchase their clothing; there is some waste, but the consequences of any folly are sure to be felt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use small financial responsibilities (wages for clothing) to teach thrift and accountability; accept some waste as a learning consequence but ensure systems where students feel direct impact of choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-school arrangements to prevent relapse
rubrics_metrics.description: No little care must be taken when they go back that favorable arrangements shall be made for a start in life; neglect at this point will imperil all the fruit of our labors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for students' re-entry into home communities with favorable employment, social supports, and opportunities to apply practical skills; school training alone is insufficient without post-school opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundraising and private support to cover deficits
rubrics_metrics.description: By private charity, and government aid...there is, after allowing $30 per year for the value of the labor of each Indian, an annual deficit...This is met by individuals and societies...the entire cost of building and outfit...has been $13,726.72, all from private contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize and plan for reliance on private charity, scholarships, and fundraising to cover operational and capital costs; document per-student cost components (board, tuition, clothing) and seek sustained philanthropic support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational policy: show how resources were secured
rubrics_metrics.description: The policy of showing Indians our great guns and enormous resources is not, I believe, so wise as that of showing them how those resources were secured, letting them witness and learn the steady, thrifty habits that are at the bottom of our prosperity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach by example and demonstration of the processes and habits (thrift, steady labor) that produce prosperity rather than merely displaying wealth or power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory principle: equal civil rights for all persons within U.S. jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: In 1870, Congress declared by law that, 'All persons within the jurisdiction of the United States shall have the same right in every State and Territory to make and enforce contracts, to sue, be parties, give evidence, and to the full and equal benefit of all laws and proceedings for the security of persons and property as is enjoyed by white citizens...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret and apply statutes broadly to include Indians among 'all persons' entitled to make and enforce contracts, sue and be sued, and enjoy the full and equal benefit of laws and legal proceedings; committee urges this inclusive construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for concurrent state and federal legislation to protect Indians' rights
rubrics_metrics.description: In order...to secure the desired protection to all their rights of property and person for those Indians who reside within the limits of any State, it is very desirable, perhaps necessary, to secure separate or concurrent legislation by both the general and State governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue both federal and state/territorial legislative action as required to ensure protection of Indian person and property rights, recognizing the division of powers and jurisdictional complexities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of change in treaty policy (1871)
rubrics_metrics.description: An act of Congress, passed in 1871...declares that...in future no Indian nation or tribe within the territory of the United States shall be acknowledged or recognized as an independent nation, tribe or power, with whom the United States may contract by treaty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy and legal approaches must account for the 1871 congressional change ending treaty-making recognition; legislative and administrative protections should be framed in light of altered federal-tribal relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of U.S. criminal statutes to Indian country
rubrics_metrics.description: Other statutes provide for the punishment of certain specified crimes and offenses...and as to all other crimes it is enacted that 'the general laws of the United States as to the punishment of crimes committed at any place within the sole and exclusive jurisdiction of the United States...shall extend to the Indian country.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand and enforce the extension of general U.S. criminal law into Indian country where applicable (see Rev. Stat. secs. 2133-2157) and ensure legal protections and punishments are applied appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative strategy: federal responsibility where state action lacking
rubrics_metrics.description: It is difficult, if not impossible, to obtain from the State or Territorial Governments...any legislation favorable to the Indians...The only hope for the Indian, is in the sense of justice, and of its duty, manifested by the general government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When state or territorial legislatures are unlikely to act in Indians' favor, federal authorities should pursue protective legislation and policy; advocacy should focus on Congress and executive agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory interpretation should include Indians
rubrics_metrics.description: Your committee believe that this statute secures to the Indians very ample and valuable rights. They can perceive no valid reason why it is not applicable to them...we believe that the sound and well-established rules which govern the construction of statutes, demand such an interpretation of its language as will embrace the Indians within its benign provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt interpretive approaches that construe broad statutory language (e.g., 'all persons within the jurisdiction') to encompass Indians unless clear congressional intent excludes them; use standard rules of statutory construction favorably.
